title: One-step extension of an anchor-free run
statement: Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet on input $w$, let $a$ be an anchor state, and let $c$ be a configuration. Suppose that at time $t$ the run from $c$ is the seam configuration with state $q$ and tape words $(w_i)_{i<k}$, and that no configuration from time $0$ through time $t$ is in state $a$. If the transition from $q$, for every scanned input symbol and tuple of work-tape symbols, is the silent action that leaves the input head and work tapes fixed and enters state $r$, where neither $q$ nor $r$ is $a$, then at time $t+1$ the run is the seam configuration with state $r$ and the same tape words, and no configuration through time $t+1$ is in state $a$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean multi-tape machine, input $w$, anchor state $a$, and starting configuration $c$
Duration $t$ and seam configuration at time $t$ with state $q$ and tape words
Anchor-free run at all times from $0$ through $t$
Transition from $q$ is the specified silent stationary action for every scanned-symbol tuple
replaced:
If an anchor-free run of length $t$ ends on a canonical word seam in a
non-anchor state whose transition is the silent dispatch to another
non-anchor state, then the run of length $t+1$ ends on the same word seam
in the new state and is still anchor-free.
